issues.description: The sphere-intersection function has inconsistent identifiers between the header and the implementation/usage in the template repository: template header example_program/src/ray_sphere_intersect.h declares a prototype named check_sphere_hit(const float *origin, const float *dir, const float *center, const float radius); however the implementation in example_program/src/ray_sphere_intersect.cpp defines bool ray_sphere_intersect(const float *origin, const float *dir, const float *center, const float radius) and callers in main.cpp invoke ray_sphere_intersect(...). This mismatch means callers include a header that does not declare the function they call, causing compilation errors and confusing students about which symbol to implement or use. (The solution repository already uses the consistent name ray_sphere_intersect in its header, implementation, and callers.)
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the function identifier across header, implementation, and callers. For the template, update example_program/src/ray_sphere_intersect.h to declare: bool ray_sphere_intersect(const float *origin, const float *dir, const float *center, const float radius); so it matches the implementation and the calls in main.cpp. Alternatively, rename the implementation and all call sites to check_sphere_hit(...) if that name is preferred. Ensure header, .cpp, and all callers use the same function name and signature so the project compiles and students clearly know which symbol to implement/use.
